##### Project general facts

London Square Wandsworth Common is a residential community of apartments and family houses arranged around a landscaped public park. Designed by Assael Architecture in a warm red-brick style, it brings together the Hawthorn, Birch, Willow and Beech apartment buildings with one, two and three-bedroom homes, alongside The Residences, a collection of semi-detached and detached four and five-bedroom houses, and a small terrace of townhouses.

Every home has its own private outdoor space, from balconies and terraces in the apartments to private gardens in the houses. Residents share communal landscaped gardens and secure cycle storage, while The Residences offer driveway parking with electric vehicle charging. A large public park lies right on the doorstep, with community gardens, a pavilion and café, a children's play area, a sports ground, an amphitheatre and wetlands with walking routes.

Apartments feature open-plan kitchen, living and dining areas with timber-effect flooring laid in a herringbone pattern, handleless fitted kitchens with integrated appliances, and en-suite bathrooms to principal bedrooms in larger layouts. The houses add shaker-style kitchens, utility and pantry rooms, garden rooms, dressing areas and generous bedrooms over several floors. Homes are delivered unfurnished, leaving owners free to style the interiors to their taste.

##### Parking

Private parking.

##### Location description and benefits

Wandsworth Common is a leafy residential area of South West London, known for its large open green spaces, village-style high streets and family atmosphere. The neighbourhood sits between Earlsfield, Tooting and Balham, with Wandsworth Common and Clapham Common close by and Battersea Park within easy reach.

Wandsworth Common, Earlsfield and Tooting Bec stations connect the area to central London by rail and the Northern line, giving quick access to Clapham Junction, Waterloo, Victoria and the City. Bellevue Road and Garratt Lane offer independent cafés, restaurants and boutiques, while Southside Shopping Centre covers everyday high street brands. The area is home to a wide choice of highly rated primary and secondary schools, as well as well-regarded independent schools.

South West London is one of the capital's most sought-after family markets, supported by strong demand from professionals and families drawn to its green spaces and schools. Property in the area is available on both leasehold and freehold tenure, appealing to owner-occupiers and buy-to-let investors seeking steady rental demand.
